feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry (#927)

* feat: add opt-out crash reporting via sentry

The app was blind in production. The panic hook wrote crashes.log and the
diagnostics zip could export it, but both needed the user to notice a failure
and file an issue by hand. React errors caught by a boundary never reached the
window at all, so they were invisible even in principle.

Desktop app only. The extension keeps its AMO data_collection_permissions of
['none'] and the landing site keeps its no-third-party-JS origin invariant.

Consent is Rust-owned rather than a renderer preference: sentry::init has to run
before tauri::Builder, because sentry-rust-minidump forks the crash-reporter
process at startup and panic = "abort" leaves nothing in-process able to flush a
crash. There is no WebView at that point, so no localStorage to read.

Transmission requires enabled && consentShown, not just enabled. The default is
on, but nothing is sent until the setup wizard has actually shown the choice — a
default nobody saw is not consent, and that gap is where privacy claims break.
A user who never finishes onboarding never reports anything.

Every outgoing event is serialized, passed through the same redact_token
pipeline the diagnostics bundle uses, and deserialized — whole-event rather than
field-by-field, because a field list is a denylist that rots as the SDK adds
fields. send_default_pii is off and server_name is overridden, since the SDK
otherwise sends the machine hostname.

The DSN is baked by build.rs from an env var set only in the signed release job
and read with option_env!, so local builds, contributor clones and every CI
check compile to None and cannot transmit.

This reverses a published promise: the privacy policy named Sentry as absent in
three places and ADR-0005 defined the boundary as "no telemetry". ADR-0005 gains
an eighth egress class, ADR-0020 records the decision, and all twelve claim
sites are rewritten — including Footer.tsx, whose "no server-side copy, deleting
locally deletes it everywhere" became false, and /privacy, which is the policy
URL filed with both stores and now separates desktop collection from extension
non-collection.

* fix: classify the crash-reporting module in the architecture layers

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: resolve the crash-reporting consent directory exactly once

Review found the feature could never activate. init() ran before
tauri::Builder and resolved the consent file through
platform::config::data_dir(), which at that moment falls back to $HOME/.ajh
because AJH_DATA_DIR is only exported later, inside setup(). The privacy
commands meanwhile wrote through app.path().app_data_dir(). Consent was
written to one directory and read from another, so no user choice was ever
observed — and it failed silently, since a missing file is indistinguishable
from "user said no".

Cache the first resolution in a OnceLock and funnel load/save/clear through
it, so both sides agree by construction rather than by two call sites
happening to resolve alike. The commands no longer take an AppHandle at all.

Adds a regression test pinning that every accessor shares one resolved
directory and that a save() is observable through load().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: stop transmission on factory reset and permit the sentry plugin

Two findings from the second review pass.

Factory reset cleared the persisted consent file but left the in-memory client
bound, so a user who had consented kept transmitting for the rest of the
session immediately after performing what reads as a full privacy wipe — the
reset does not restart the process. Now unbinds alongside the clear, mirroring
the opt-out path in privacy_set_crash_reporting.

The plugin was registered without a capability entry. Its browser side forwards
events to Rust over invoke, and those commands (envelope, breadcrumb) are
permission-gated in Tauri 2, so without "sentry:default" every renderer error
would have been denied at the IPC boundary and silently never reported — half
the feature dead while looking wired up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: use the ureq transport and document where consent is stored

Third review pass.

Drop sentry's default features. The default transport is reqwest + native-tls,
and sentry 0.42 pins reqwest 0.12 — a second copy alongside the app's 0.13, in
a binary optimized hard for size. ureq is lighter and also more correct here:
the reqwest transport needs tokio, but the minidump supervisor is a bare forked
process with no async runtime to send on. Verified reqwest 0.12 is gone from
the tree and ureq 3.3 replaces it. The reported actix-web integration was not
actually in the tree — defaults never enabled it.

The module claimed the consent file sits next to the other app data. It does
not: it lives where data_dir() resolves before Tauri starts, which in a default
install is $HOME/.ajh, not the per-OS app-data dir. That placement is forced —
sentry::init has no AppHandle, and the init cannot move into setup because the
minidump supervisor re-executes everything above its own call in the forked
child. Corrected the claim rather than the location, and recorded the
consequence: deleting the app-data dir by hand leaves this file, though it
holds two booleans and the factory reset clears it.

ci: add a blocking accessibility gate for the landing site (#925)

* ci: add a blocking accessibility gate for the landing site

PR #924 fixed every WCAG A/AA violation on the landing site and published
/accessibility, a page that states those results. Nothing re-checked them,
so the fixes could regress silently and the statement would start lying.
Every scan in that PR ran from throwaway scripts under apps/desktop, the
only place @axe-core/playwright already resolved.

check-a11y.mjs serves the built out/ with node:http, drives headless
Chromium and axe-core, and scans every route discovered by globbing
out/**/*.html rather than a hardcoded list - a hardcoded list is the exact
failure mode the #924 review flagged, where a new route had to be added by
hand in four places. It runs on pull requests inside the existing test job,
reusing the Chromium already installed there.

It blocks rather than warns. That differs from the three desktop a11y
checks on purpose: those stay advisory because their surface is not clean
yet, whereas this baseline is already 0, so anything it finds is a
regression against a public claim.

Auto-discovery immediately found 13 routes rather than the 9 previously
scanned, and three had never been checked:

- /404 and /_not-found are clean.
- /mission-control failed contrast at 4.03:1 on row-title links. Fixed with
  --doc-accent-text, the token docs-tokens.css already defines for this
  case, at a specificity that beats the .doc-shell base rule; now 5.7:1.
- /benchmarks/ fails contrast and lacks a lang attribute, but is generated
  by benchmark-action and overwritten on every push-to-main perf run, so it
  cannot be fixed in-repo. It is excluded by name, with the reason and both
  violations recorded in EXCLUDED_ROUTES, and the gate logs the exclusion
  rather than skipping silently.

The statement is updated to match: 12 covered routes instead of 9, the
/mission-control fix, the gate itself under what is in place, and
/benchmarks/ disclosed as a known barrier that is excluded, not passing.
Every prior disclosure stands - both surfaces remain partially conformant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: contain the a11y gate's static server to out/

CodeQL flagged two high-severity path-traversal sinks in the gate's own
static server: resolveFile stripped leading slashes but nothing stopped
../ escaping out/ through join(), so /../../../package.json resolved
outside the served root.

Real risk is negligible - the server is loopback-only on an ephemeral port
for the seconds a scan takes, reachable only by the Playwright instance the
script itself launches - but the alert is correct rather than a false
positive, and the containment check is three lines. Resolving each
candidate and requiring it to sit inside out/ is the fix, not a
suppression.

Verified against the running server: /../../../package.json,
/..%2f..%2fpackage.json and /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/package.json all 404, while
/privacy and /fonts/fonts.css still serve 200 and all 12 routes still scan
clean - so no legitimate asset path was caught by the filter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: serve the a11y gate from an allowlist instead of built paths

The previous commit added a containment check after building the path with
join(), and CodeQL still flagged both sinks - correctly, because the
tainted request path reached the path expression before anything validated
it. Sanitising a sink is weaker than not having one.

The server now walks out/ once at startup and serves only from the
resulting Map of real files, keyed by the URL that serves them. The request
path never reaches a path expression; it only ever looks up a key, so
traversal is impossible by construction rather than by a check a later
refactor could reorder or drop. It also removes the isFile stat dance,
since only real files are ever indexed - a route whose .html sits beside a
same-named directory of RSC payloads can no longer resolve to the
directory.

Verified against the running server: /../../../package.json,
/..%2f..%2fpackage.json and /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/package.json all 404, while /,
/privacy, /privacy.html, /fonts/fonts.css and /benchmarks/ all serve 200
and all 12 routes still scan clean.

Adds /accessibility, a WAI-model statement covering all three surfaces: the
landing site, the desktop app and the browser extension.

visible ring, no overflow at 320px under reduced motion. It reuses
privacy.css rather than adding a stylesheet, and is linked from the shared

* chore: add robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt to the landing site

The static site shipped with no crawl metadata at all: no robots.txt, no
sitemap, and nothing aimed at LLM crawlers.

- robots.ts allows everything except /mission-control (a live GitHub-API
  dashboard that already sets robots index false on the page) and points at
  the sitemap.
- sitemap.ts lists the 8 indexable routes, matching each page's own canonical.
  No lastModified/priority: Google ignores priority and a build-time timestamp
  would churn the file on every deploy.
- public/llms.txt follows the llms.txt convention (H1, summary blockquote, key
  facts, Pages, Optional). Adoption by AI crawlers is currently unproven, but
  the file is static and costs one bullet per new page.

Both metadata routes need a force-static dynamic export: Next 16 defaults them
to dynamic and output export rejects that outright.

Verified: typecheck, build (out/robots.txt + out/sitemap.xml + out/llms.txt all
emitted), check:parity, and lint:strict --max-warnings 0 all pass.

feat: revoke extension pairing over the bridge on token rotation (#895)

* feat: revoke extension pairing over the bridge on token rotation

Rotating the pairing token (Settings -> Regenerate, or a factory reset) left
live authenticated sockets running and the connected count up, and a
reconnecting extension only saw the deliberately silent failed-handshake close
- indistinguishable from a crashed app - so it retried the dead token forever
and never returned to its pairing view.

Adds a desktop -> extension `token.revoked` frame (TS constants + zod enum and
the Rust msg mirror, in lockstep). BridgeState::regenerate_token now signals
every live connection task, zeroes the live-connection count, then swaps the
secret, all inside the token lock so no handshake can authenticate against the
old token and miss the revoke. Only an ALREADY-AUTHENTICATED socket is sent the
frame; an unauthenticated one closes silently as before, preserving the
no-token-oracle invariant (ADR-0010). The frame carries no payload and no token
material.

The extension drops its stored token through the same local un-pair path the
popup's Unpair button uses, skips the backoff loop, and re-probes once unpaired
so the popup lands on the pairing view. Old extensions ignore an unknown wire
type, so no protocol-version bump is needed.

Also moves the msg constant table into its own module (the addition pushed
extension_bridge/mod.rs past the R8 hard LOC cap) and mentions re-pairing in the
factory-reset confirm copy (en + de).

* fix: honor token.revoked only on an authenticated bridge session

The `handshakeFrame` intercept is a step-in-flight latch, not an auth check:

destroy the stored pairing credential; the revoke close path's backoff reset
made that loopable. The pre-hello window and the no-token attach (which reaches

feat: offline geonames geocoding with photon fallback (#893)

* feat: offline geonames geocoding with photon fallback

Retire the public-Nominatim autocomplete: its usage policy forbids
autocomplete, and its throttling silently degraded the picker to zero
suggestions.

A bundled GeoNames index is now the primary source. The new geodata
directory under the Tauri crate carries cities15000 (34k rows, gzipped
TSV) plus countryInfo (252 rows), compiled in with include_bytes! and
include_str! — no network at build time, no new table, no new crate. The
index builds once behind a LazyLock and folds every search key through
the existing cluster normalize fold, so diacritic equivalence cannot
drift.

Ranking is exact country name, then exact city name, then prefix hits
(country prefix, city prefix, exact alternate spelling), then alternate
prefixes; population decides within a tier, so "ber" yields Berlin
rather than Bermuda and "muenchen" yields Munich.

Photon (OpenStreetMap/ODbL) is the fallback, reached only when the index
returns nothing for a query of at least three characters. A network or
parse failure degrades to no suggestions, exactly as before.

The suggest() signature and result shape are unchanged (display, lat,
lon, countryCode; capped at 5; deduped), so geocode_suggest,
LocationInput and the autopilot country-code backfill need no changes.

GeoNames is CC BY 4.0 and Photon serves ODbL data, so attribution ships
in Settings, About (en and de) and in the geodata README, ADR-0005 and
the scraping knowledge doc. Regenerate the assets with pnpm gen:geonames.

* fix: resolve country codes and endonyms exactly in offline geocoding

Country rows were indexed by English name only, so a typed country code or
endonym prefix-matched an unrelated city and returned five confident-looking
rows: usa/us gave Uşak (TR), uk gave Ukraine, de gave DR Congo, gb gave Gboko
(NG), schweiz gave Schweizer-Reneke (ZA). Callers take the first suggestion's
country code, so entering "Schweiz" persisted za — a live Adzuna market, i.e. a
silent switch to South African jobs.

Three changes close it. countries.tsv now carries ISO3 (countryInfo column 1),
and both ISO codes are matched exact-only, never as a prefix. A small curated
endonym table (deutschland, schweiz, suisse, uk, espana, …) lives in Rust rather
than the asset, so regenerating from upstream cannot wipe it. And the online
fallback is gated on match quality instead of non-emptiness: the index now
reports whether anything matched a key exactly, and an inexact result no longer
vetoes the Photon lookup that would have answered correctly. Inexact hits use a
higher query-length floor than misses do, so partial typing ("ber", "berli")
still stays offline.

The picker's own "City, Country" label is retried against the text before the
first comma, so re-opening the dropdown resolves offline instead of always
going online.

The UI package no longer ships a geocoder: onFetchSuggestions is required on
both useGeocoding and LocationInput, and the Nominatim defaultFetch is deleted.
It was reachable — the published Storybook rendered LocationInput without the
prop, issuing live browser-side autocomplete traffic with no user agent.

Also: cap the query length before building a third-party URL, correct the
index-cost comments with measured numbers, drop the postcode claim from the
story placeholder, and pin all of the above with tests, including the Photon
request shape, user agent and timeout against a local mock server.

* fix: make the geocoding fallback and index degradation testable

The Photon branch of suggest() could not be reached from a test: photon()
hardcoded the endpoint, so every suggest() test returned at the offline
early-return and the merge rule — Photon replaces a weak offline hit, an
empty or failed Photon answer leaves the offline rows alone — was asserted
nowhere. A suggest_at(endpoint, query) seam mirrors the existing photon_at
one, and three mock-server tests now pin each branch. The tests that rely on
an offline early-return also assert the query really is an exact index hit,
so asset drift fails them instead of quietly making CI issue live requests.

Index construction gets the same treatment: parse() and decode_cities() are
split out of load(), and their degradation arms are covered — corrupt gzip,
short and long rows, non-numeric coordinates, empty names, malformed country
codes, unparseable population, a duplicate country code, and an alias whose
country is absent from the asset.

Confidence is now read only from the rows that survive into the returned
suggestions. An exact hit ranked below the cap is invisible to the caller,
so letting it set the flag vetoed the fallback on the strength of a row
nobody was shown.

Also in this round: the index is warmed from setup on a blocking thread,
since derive_country_code's timeout cannot interrupt a synchronous build;
queries in scripts the asset cannot hold skip the length floors instead of
being permanently unanswerable; the last 32 lookups are memoized, and only
when non-empty so a transient failure is retried; country codes are checked
for ASCII letters rather than byte length; both assets carry a recorded
SHA-256 and fetch date that a test asserts; the egress ADR states the
exemption that makes a user-typed lookup different from enrichment; and the
attribution line is legible enough for a credit we are required to show.

the clips that existed at the first touch (segment 0). Every later scene
stayed on its poster forever. loadClip now primes a clip the moment it is
created once the user has interacted, and the gesture listeners stay
registered so a later touch primes anything still unprimed (which also covers
a first touch landing while segment 0's fetch is in flight). A per-segment
primed flag keeps that to one play() per clip.

(hover:none) and (pointer:coarse) matches iPadOS, Android tablets and touch
laptops at any width, so every tablet was permanently served the 720x1280
crf28 portrait phone encodes and desktop CSS then cropped them. Mobile now
means a coarse pointer AND a phone-sized screen, tested on the screen's short
side so rotation cannot flip it, and the decision is frozen at mount so
posters and clips can never come from different sets.

Also bounds clip-failure recovery: a video error listener resets the segment
back to its poster instead of latching loading forever, and a per-segment try
counter caps retries at 3 so a dead URL cannot refetch on every scroll tick.

Deviations D2-D5 recorded in ADR-0019's engine deviation log; a new jsdom test
guards them across re-vendors.

* fix: prime world clips on trackpad ipads and guard stale clip errors

Applies the frontend-reviewer advisories on the /world engine.

The priming gate moves off `coarse` onto a mount-time
`navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0`. Since iPadOS 13.4 an iPad with a Magic
Keyboard or trackpad reports hover:hover + pointer:fine, so a coarse gate
skipped priming there while WebKit still gated media loading on a gesture —
posters forever on exactly that configuration. maxTouchPoints covers every
touch-capable browser; a Windows touch laptop just takes a harmless muted
play/pause and a real desktop reports 0 and never primes. `coarse` still
gates the particle drop and the URL-bar resize guard.

The video error handler now starts with an identity guard. Media elements can
error more than once and a discarded element outlives its replacement, so a
late error was resetting the segment while the live clip was still mounted —
freezing it and stacking a second video into the scene on the next tick. The
teardown also revokes the discarded blob URL; live clips keep theirs by
design, but a failing segment was leaking one multi-MB blob per retry.
play() returning a non-promise now pauses immediately instead of leaving the
clip running under the scrubber.

Tests go 12 to 16: a non-touch desktop never-prime lock, a trackpad-iPad
priming case, the non-promise pause, and the stale-error clobber. ADR-0019's
deviation log records the canTouch rationale, the identity guard and revoke,
and names eps as the third consumer of the frozen isMobile.

* fix: guard every world clip listener against a replaced element

Applies the PR #890 CI review advisories on the /world engine.

The identity guard added for the error listener covered only that listener.
A media element keeps firing after the segment has torn it down and replaced
it, so a late loadedmetadata from a discarded video set s.ready while the live
clip had no metadata at all, and raf() then scrubbed it against the
duration || 1 fallback; a late seeked hid the poster to reveal a video that
was never painted. All the listeners now share one liveness check.

Teardown clears the source and re-runs the load algorithm before revoking the
blob URL — a detached element can hold decoder resources until its source is
dropped, and the retry path makes up to three per segment. Priming gains a
primeTries cap mirroring tries, since a refusal deliberately clears primed and
a browser refusing muted playback outright would otherwise take a fresh play()
on every pointerdown for the life of the page.

The header MOBILE block no longer lists the particle drop and the URL-bar
resize guard as phone-tier behaviour: both key off the coarse pointer alone
and apply to tablets, which contradicted the inline comments and the ADR.

because every test stubs rAF away: one hand-rolled frame at a scroll offset
where the lerped step falls between the two seek thresholds, so a tablet
mount seeks and a phone mount coalesces. Also covers the late-loadedmetadata
guard and the prime cap, and documents the test file's cross-mount coupling.

* fix: return a disposer from the world engine mount

Applies the CodeRabbit review on PR #890.

mountScrollWorld returned nothing and never unregistered: six window
listeners, a self-rescheduling rAF loop and every clip's blob URL outlived
the mount, so StrictMode's dev double-invoke or a client-side route change
stacked a whole second engine over the first, driving detached DOM forever.
It now returns an idempotent disposer that cancels the pending frame, removes
the listeners, releases each clip and empties the container; read() and raf()
early-return once torn down, and a clip whose fetch resolves after teardown is
dropped instead of appended to a dead scene. An empty config returns a no-op
disposer rather than undefined. The injected style element stays: it is
id-guarded and may be shared with another live mount.

mountedRef latch that only existed because teardown was impossible, so /world
no longer has to be entered via a full navigation. scrub-engine.d.ts carries
the new return type.

Clip release is now one shared helper used by both the error path and the
disposer, and it pauses before clearing the source so a detached element
cannot sit on decoder resources.

Tests: dispose every mount in afterEach rather than relying only on per-mount
asset-path scoping, restore the stubbed screen dimensions, cover the classifier
threshold from both sides, and add teardown coverage.

The ADR deviation log gains D6 for the disposer and swaps the copied
thresholds in D2 to D4 for pointers at the symbols that own them.

computed overflow-y to auto — making .doc-shell a scroll container. The
sticky panel then resolved against .doc-shell (which never scrolls
internally) instead of the viewport, so it never pinned and scrolled
away with the page.

establishing a scroll container, so descendant sticky pins resolve
against the viewport again. Verified in-browser: pinned across the full
runway, belt scrubs horizontally, no horizontal scrollbar.

fix(ui): flush a pending RichTextEditor edit on unmount instead of dropping it (#841)

* fix(ui): flush a pending RichTextEditor edit on unmount instead of dropping it

The unmount effect is commented "Flush any pending debounce on unmount so the
last edit is never lost", but its body only cleared the timer — `emit` was
never called, so the pending markdown was discarded.

`RichTextEditor` is rendered conditionally (Preview / Edit / Source in
EditableOutput), so switching view unmounts it. Type, then click Preview within
ONCHANGE_DEBOUNCE_MS (200ms) and the last edit is gone: the parent-owned
`value` still holds the pre-keystroke markdown, the preview/PDF renders stale
text, and re-entering Edit re-parses the stale value. No error, no indication.
The same loss happens on any unmount of the surrounding panel inside the
debounce window — the ordinary "type, then immediately click away" pattern.

Capture the pending document synchronously in `onUpdate` (a ProseMirror node is
immutable, so it is just a pointer copy) and serialize THAT in the cleanup,
rather than reaching into an editor Tiptap may already have destroyed by the
time this component's cleanup runs. The timer path clears the ref before
emitting, so the two paths can never double-emit.

`emitDoc` is `useCallback([])`-stable, so `emit` stays stable and the existing
`useImperativeHandle(ref, …, [editor, emit])` dependency list is unaffected.

* test(ui): make the unmount-flush suite deterministic

The new suite was red on CI at the previous commit. Two independent causes,
both in the test setup rather than the production change:

- The editor's initial-content load is itself a transaction, so a mounted
  editor schedules one debounced emit on its own. Under real timers that
  mount emit could fire before the "nothing emitted yet" assertion on a
  slower runner. Drain and clear it explicitly before the edit under test.

- jsdom implements no layout, so `Range.getClientRects` is undefined and
  ProseMirror's coordsAtPos -> singleRect throws an unhandled
  "target.getClientRects is not a function" from scrollToSelection on every
  editor transaction. Stub `Range.getClientRects`/`getBoundingClientRect`
  in the shared jsdom setup alongside the existing scrollIntoView stub, so
  the "still emits exactly once" assertion is no longer polluted by it.

fix(scraper): delegate board location filtering to the central location_filter (#835)

* fix(scraper): match a 'City, Country' location label segment-wise

The location box normally holds the geocode picker's "<city>, <country>"
label — `commands::geocoding` builds it exactly so "the UI only ever shows
'City, Country'", and both entry points (jobs ScrapeFilters, autopilot
StepTarget) write `suggestion.display` straight into `location`.

The two boards that filter location client-side required that WHOLE label to
appear as one contiguous substring of the board's own location text. No board
writes it that way:

  The Muse        "New York, NY"            vs request "New York, United States"
  GermanTechJobs  "Karl-Marx-Allee 1, Berlin" / "Munich, Bayern"
                                            vs request "Berlin, Germany"

so the filter dropped every row and the board reported 0 results for any
picked city. Typing free text without picking a suggestion still worked,
which is why it survives manual testing.

Match segment-wise instead: any non-empty comma-separated part of the request
appearing in the haystack is enough. Conservative — it errs toward keeping,
mirroring the engine's own `location_filter`, which already tokenizes the
request and keeps on any token hit for this exact reason.

- adds `common::location_matches`, shared by both call sites
- extracts `germantechjobs::matches_gtj_filters` from `search()`'s `retain`
  so tests drive the real predicate instead of a copy that could diverge
  (same reasoning as The Muse's `apply_filters`)

Single-segment requests behave exactly as before.

* fix(scraper): delegate board location filtering to the central location_filter

Reworks the fix per review. The first version added a board-local segment-wise
matcher (`location_matches`); this removes board-local LOCATION filtering from
the three `supports_location() == false` boards entirely and lets the engine's
central `location_filter` be the single authority — the reviewer's preferred
direction, and the one the issue points at.

Why this is correct and strictly better than a second local matcher:

- The Muse, Comeet and GermanTechJobs are all non-location boards, so the engine
  already runs `location_filter` on their output both as a live gate
  (`KeepItemByBoardFn`) and as a post-hoc safety net. Board-local location
  filtering was redundant with it.
- The central filter is diaeresis/exonym-aware (München/Munich, Köln/Cologne via
  the curated table + DIN-5007-2 folding) and conservative (keeps remote /
  empty / unknown, and a country-code-only request is inert). A raw
  case-insensitive board-local matcher had none of that and, running BEFORE the
  central filter, produced false drops the central filter is designed to rescue.
- The original 0-results bug is still fixed: `location_spec()` feeds the picker's
  "<city>, <country>" label into the central filter, which TOKENISES it (it does
  not require the whole label as one substring), so a geocode-picked city keeps
  its rows via the central filter alone.

Changes:
- common.rs: `matches_filters` is now keyword-only (drops the `location` param);
  `location_matches` is deleted.
- germantechjobs: `matches_gtj_filters` is keyword-only; the unused `loc` local
  is removed.
- The Muse / Comeet call sites pass query only.
- Tests updated across common/themuse/germantechjobs: the board-local location
  assertions are replaced with ones pinning that these boards no longer drop on
  location (delegated to the central filter, whose own exonym/diacritic behaviour
  is unit-tested in engine::location_filter).

Known limitation (unchanged by this PR, now consistent across all non-location
boards): because `location_spec()` stores the whole label in `city`, the central
filter also tokenises the country segment, so "Munich, Germany" keeps a
"Frankfurt, Germany" row. That is a central-filter property shared by every
non-location board, not something this PR introduces; tightening it is a separate
change to `location_filter`/`location_spec`.
